experiment: T01 — Playwright (raw, scripted) vs existing CDP browser harness

armA_browser_exec.note: fill_input+form.submit sent empty value twice; JS value-set worked

notes: Arm A = existing CDP browser harness via browser_exec; token cost = main-model turns, not separately metered. Arm B = raw Playwright 1.5x (installed pip --user on worker; chromium already present) — zero model tokens per run once the script exists. Same outputs on all three tasks. Key difference is not speed but who writes the selectors: harness = model writes selectors live (retry cost), Playwright = selectors written once, deterministic forever.
verdict: Split by stability: fixed/repeatable jobs (clipping scrapers, daily digests) -> scripted Playwright on the worker; exploratory, login-walled or one-off jobs -> browser harness. Playwright MCP not in Hermes connector catalog; raw library gives same capability without the wrapper.
